comparison: Both evaluate GNU interactions with BIC-C and ME31B (C8-C11). OpenEval also includes PP2A interaction (C12) while peer review groups C12 with C8-C11. Both find evidence SUPPORTED, with peer reviewers praising the high-quality mass spectrometry and immunoprecipitation data.
OpenEval evaluates PP2A interaction (C12) separately as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups C12 with other interaction claims (C8-C11) and finds them SUPPORTED without specific critique of the PP2A data.

Both address SAM domain requirement for BIC-C interaction. OpenEval evaluates C13-C15 as SUPPORTED with convergent evidence. Peer review finds C13 UNCERTAIN, requesting quantification and normalization due to concerns about GNU protein levels in IPs. This represents a key disagreement.

Both address SAM domain requirement (C14-C15). OpenEval groups these with C13 and finds all SUPPORTED. Peer review evaluates C14-C15 separately as SUPPORTED, accepting the SAM domain requirement without critique.

Both evaluate GNU∆SAM phenotype and function (C16-C18). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED but groups C19-C20 with these claims, requesting improved figure presentation for giant nuclei visualization.

OpenEval evaluates BIC-C decrease and GNU persistence in gnu∆SAM (C19-C20) as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these with C16-C18 and finds all SUPPORTED, with only presentation concerns about figure clarity.

Perfect match on claims C21-C24 regarding GNU granular localization and dispersal. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note data are 'clear and convincing' with only presentation requests for high magnification insets.

Perfect match on claims C25-C26 regarding co-localization quantification. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept the heterogeneity findings with only presentation concerns about color reproduction and image magnification.
Perfect match on claim C27 regarding GNU9A altered localization. Both find SUPPORTED without substantive critique of the data validity.
Perfect match on claims C28-C31 regarding BIC-C requirement for GNU localization. Both find SUPPORTED with only presentation improvement requests from peer reviewers.
Perfect match on claims C32-C33 regarding selective effects on BIC-C versus ME31B localization. Both find SUPPORTED without challenge to data validity.
OpenEval evaluates persistent GNU-BIC-C interaction (C34) as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups C34 with C35-C36 and finds all SUPPORTED, with only technical clarifications requested about band sizes.
OpenEval evaluates differential CYCB effects (C35-C36) as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these with C34 and finds all SUPPORTED, accepting the evidence against sequestration model.

Both address authors' synthesis and model (C37-C40). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these with C42, C44-C45 and finds SUPPORTED, acknowledging some interpretations are speculative but not diminishing enthusiasm for the work.
OpenEval evaluates GNU structure and GNU9A mechanism (C41-C42) as SUPPORTED with C42 noted as speculative. Peer review groups C42 with broader model claims (C37-C40, C44-C45) and finds SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates temporal model (C44-C45) as SUPPORTED but requiring further investigation. Peer review groups these with broader model claims and finds SUPPORTED, accepting the interpretations as consistent with data.

Perfect match on claims C46-C48 regarding GNU-containing granules as distinct subpopulation. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers suggest citing additional literature on granule heterogeneity, supporting rather than challenging the finding.

Perfect match on claims C63-C64 regarding GNU degradation mechanism. OpenEval finds UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of C64. Peer review finds SUPPORTED, accepting both the observation (C63) and speculation (C64) without critique.

Both address background claims from literature (C1-C7). OpenEval evaluates these separately as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups all background claims (C1-C7, C41, C43, C49-C62, C65-C67) together and finds SUPPORTED.

Both address extensive background and comparative biology claims. OpenEval evaluates C43, C49-C62, C65-C67 as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups all background claims including C1-C7 and C41 together and finds SUPPORTED without challenge.
